Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Sri Lanka's second innings as the two openers for the Lankans, Dimuth Karunaratne and Lahiru Thirimanne make their way out to the middle. The West Indies players are out on the field too as the spread to take their fielding positions. Kemar Roach to start with the ball for the West Indies.

So that ends West Indies' first innings. They batted for just 2 overs on Day 3 before getting bowled out. They would though hold the psychological advantage over Sri Lanka by stretching the lead beyond 100 runs. Rahkeem Cornwall was dismissed first in the morning as he could manage to add just 1 run to his overnight score of 60 runs. Fernando was the one who finished it up with a couple of wickets. Overall, West Indies would be pretty happy with their performance with the bat as they were not in a position of even getting a lead of 50 runs at one stage. but thanks to the 90-run stand between Cornwall and Da Silva. Lakmal was the star for the visitors as he took a 5-fer. Now, it is up to the Sri Lankan batsmen to get them off to a strong start as they first look to wipe off the deficit without damage and then look to set a target for the West Indies to chase, Join us for  Sri Lanka's batting in the second essay on the other side of this short break.
Review taken! Shannon Gabriel is adjudged out and he takes the review. The replays roll in. Ultra Edge shows no bat involved and the Ball Tracker shows THREE REDS!

OUT! LBW! That's it! Gabriel goes and that's the end of the innings! Fernando does not take long to finish things off. Full ball on middle, Gabriel looks to flick but misses and gets rapped on the pads. An appeal is made and the finger has gone up. Gabriel takes the review but it seems in desperation. The Ultra Edge rolls in and it shows that there is no bat while the Ball Tracker shows that all reds. WEST INDIES ALL OUT FOR 271, LEADING BY 102 RUNS.
Back of a length ball on middle, Gabriel tucks it to mid-wicket.
Full ball on middle, Gabriel flicks it to square leg.
Shannon Gabriel is the last man in for the West Indies.

OUT! CLEANED HIM UP! This time the inswing does the trick! The big man, Rahkeem Cornwall has to go. Fernando gets his first wicket of the innings! Full ball on off, it swings in sharply. Rahkeem looks to go for the big booming drive but misses and the ball shatters the stumps behind.
Good length ball on middle, Cornwall pushes it to mid on.
That came in very sharply! Good length ball around off, angling in. Roach looks to defend but gets beaten on the inside edge. The keeper fails to collect and a bye is taken.
Who will bowl from the other end? Vishwa Fernando to bowl from the other end.
Good length ball on middle and leg, Cornwall looks to drive but gets hit on the thigh pad. No run.
Fullish on the pads, Cornwall flicks it to mid-wicket.
On middle, pushed to mid on.
Full on the pads, Roach flicks it to fine leg for a single.
Full on off, Roach is solid in defense.
Lakmal starts with a good length ball on the pads, Cornwall flicks it to deep square leg for a single. WEST INDIES LEAD BY 100 RUNS!
We are all set to begin. The overnight batsmen for West Indies, Rahkeem Cornwall and Kemar Roach are out in the middle and so are the Sri Lankan players. Suranga Lakmal to start with the ball.

Darren Ganga is down for the pitch report along with Courtney Walsh. He says that there will be lateral movement and variable bounce.  There will be a great challenge for the batsmen to play their shots on this surface. Walsh further says that Jason Holder would be the one who would look to exploit the variable bounce with his height and seam movement.

Joshua Da Silva is down for the chat. He says that he just asked Cornwall to back himself and it is home ground so he knows the conditions. He mentions that he just does his job and looks to put pressure back on the opposition. He further says that his dismissal was at the wrong time and he says that the shot he played was not needed. Ends by saying that the pitch is still not good for batting as there is still some movement and variable bounce.

2 wickets in hand! 99 runs ahead! With this scenario welcome to Day 3 of this first Test between West Indies and Sri Lanka. Having folded for just 169 runs in their first innings, Sri Lanka did well to come back with the ball as Suranga Lakmal was the star with the ball as he took 5 wickets as they had West Indies tottering at 171/7 but a 90 run stand between Rahkeem Cornwall and Joshua Da Silva robbed them away of the momentum as West Indies took a handy lead of 99 runs and with two wickets left and Cornwall going strong at the crease they would hope to add a few more runs to their tally. Sri Lanka on the other hand would look to wipe out the West Indies innings quickly and then bat sensibly to post a winning total in this first Test. Who will come out on top? Stay tuned as we bring all the live coverage as the action unfolds on Day 3.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

That is that on Day 2! We witnessed some absorbing cricket where the momentum swung both ways. West Indies though managed to get their noses in front towards the end and Sri Lanka have a bit of catch up to do again. The morning session of the 'moving day' is going to be very critical. The action begins at 1000 local (1400 GMT). Do join us then. Cheers!

Rahkeem Cornwall says that he has good batting skills and he just backed himself. Tells he was confident and he told himself that he has to score. Cornwall shares that Joshua gave him confidence and told him to back himself. Cornwall feels that they are in a good position. Tells that they need to come on Day 3 and play out the first session well and further strengthen their grip on this game.

Joshua Da Silva and Rahkeem Cornwall turned out to be the saviour for West Indies as they combined for a 90-run stand for the 8th wicket. Their partnership handed back the advantage to the home team and now they will be breathing a lot comfortably. The Caribbean team has a couple of wickets in hand and more importantly, Cornwall is still unbeaten and he can add vital runs with the last two wickets. Currently, they lead by 99 runs and they would be aiming to stretch it close to 150 on Day 3. Here is the big guy, up for a quick chat...

A fantastic day of Test cricket comes to a close! It was a bit of a see-saw on Day 2. West Indies did well for most parts in the morning session but had to share the session after losing their second wicket at the fag end. The afternoon session was full of intent from Sri Lanka, as powered by Suranga Lakmal's splendid bowling, they created quick inroads. Just when the touring team hoped to capitalize and restrict West Indies' lead under 50, a partnership blossomed.
Roach manages to see off the final delivery! Floated on off, Roach defends it off the outer half of his bat but away from the man at second slip. STUMPS ON DAY 2!
Edged but with soft hands. Floated on off, Roach leans forward to defend but gets an outside edge. Luckily, it does not carry to the man at slip. One ball to see off the day.
Floated on off, Rahkeem Cornwall pushes it towards mid off and takes the risk of taking a single. Two balls to survive for Roach.
Short and wide outside off. Cornwall punches it through covers for a couple.
Tossed up on off, RC blocks it too. 4 balls to negotiate the day. Can Cornwall manage to see them off without any damage?
Floated full on off, Cornwall lunges forward and blocks it to point.
Full and fast outside off, Roach thinks to play at it but decides not to bother the ball in the end. Dot ball.
Length ball, on middle, Roach walks across the line looking to flick it away but gets hit on the pads. Niroshan Dickwella appeals loudly behind the stumps but he is the only one appealing.
Fires this one full on his stumps and Roach plays it back to the bowler.
Sharp bouncer, effort ball by Dushmantha Chameera and Roach ducks under it.

FOUR! Streaky but he will take it! Full ball on his middle and leg, a bit of shape away from the stumps and Kemar Roach gets a thick outside edge through the slips for a boundary. Lead moves on to 96.
Short of a length, comes in with the angle as he is bowling from round the stumps. Kemar Roach plays it out safely with soft hands.
Short on the pads, Cornwall tucks it to the leg side but cannot get the gap. Roach will have the strike for the start of the next over.
Flighted on off, Cornwall pushes it back to the bowler.
Tossed up on middle, Cornwall turns it to the leg side.
Flighted on off, Cornwall blocks it.
On the stumps, kept out.
Floated on off, Cornwall blocks it.
Full, fast on his pads as Kemar Roach plays it out to short mid on.
Beaten! Beautifully bowled by Dushmantha Chameera. Length ball on the fourth stump, Roach is stuck in his crease as he looks to defend it off the front foot but the ball whizzes past his bat.
Roach getting a taste of his own medicine here. Dushmantha Chameera fires a fast yorker on off, Kemar Roach manages to dig it out.
Length ball, middle stump line and blocked away by Kemar Roach.
Kemar Roach walks out to bat!

OUT! CAUGHT! Soft dismissal and Joshua Da Silva will be gutted to be dismissed in that manner. End of a brilliant knock. He deserved a fifty but will not get it, unfortunately. Short ball around off, Joshua expected it. He looks to guide it over the slip cordon but moves too far away and ends up getting a feather on it, straight to the keeper. An easy take for Dickwella and a stand that might be the one that changes the game is broken.
In the air...but drops well short of the fielder. Short ball and Rahkeem Cornwall attempts the hook shot, gets the top edge but drops short of fine leg. They cross over for a run.
Flighted on middle, Da Silva manages to block this too.
Tossed up on off, Joshua keeps it out.
On the stumps, Joshua blocks it once more.
Flighted on off, JDS defends it.
Tossed up on the stumps, Joshua defends it.
Floated on off, Joshua blocks it.
FOUR! Fighting fire with fire! Cornwall anticipates the length to be short again, gets into the position early and pummels his pull behind square leg for a cracking boundary.

Bangs it in short and on middle, Cornwall stands back with an open stance and fends it off from the upper half of his bat. It lobs in the air but drops safely on the pitch. If Chameera is bowling from this angle and looking to bounce Cornwall out, there should be a bat-pad in place. Here it comes now, a silly point.
Chameera switches to 'round the wicket and bowls a bouncer around off, Cornwall sways away. Called a WIDE for height.
Pitches it up and outside off, once again Rahkeem offers no shot.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, shaping away, Cornwall allows it through to the keeper.
Too full in length and on middle, it's worked in the gap at mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Edgy! Full and wide outside off, Joshua leans into the drive, looking to go through covers but it takes the outside half and races to the third man fence.
Rahkeem has just blocked that from his crease.
The batsman is forward as he plays it towards mid off.

FOUR! FIFTY FOR CORNWALL! His first in Test cricket and this should be the beginning of Cornwall's batting career in international cricket. He has been fantastic so far in this innings and he will try and convert this into a telling century. He gets to his fifty in style. Floated on off, Cornwall drives it beautifully through covers and reaches his milestone.
On off, kept out.
On off, Cornwall blocks it.
Flicked to the on side for a single.

FOUR! Cornwall moves to 46 off just 59 balls. This has been the coming of Rahkeem Cornwall, the batsman, in Test cricket. Flighted on off, Cornwall lofts it over mid off and gets a boundary. People who watch West Indies domestic cricket know he can bat and now he is proving it on the world stage.
Now knocks this to mid on and follows the boundary with a single.
FOUR! Wonderfully played! Short outside off, Joshua waits for it and then opens the face of the bat to place it behind backward point and away from the fielder for a boundary.
Flighted on off, JDS keeps it out.
Flighted on off, Joshua leans forward and wrists it to short mid-wicket.
Floated on middle, Joshua pushes it to mid on.
Flatter ball on his stumps, Rahkeem Cornwall plays it straight as an arrow as he defensively pushes it back to the spinner.
Slower through the air, on middle as Cornwall blocks it out.
Fuller, outside off and blocked away by Cornwall.
FOUR! Poor delivery and punished by the right-hander. Short on stumps, turning away and Rahkeem Cornwall carves it past backward point for a boundary. He moves on to 42.
Flighted ball on middle, Cornwall puts in a big stride to defend it.
Flatter ball on middle, punched to mid on by Cornwall.
NO BALL! Flighted ball on off, Rahkeem Cornwall gets a good stride forward to defend it. Another no ball for the left-arm spinner, second in two overs.
Maiden for Dhananjaya de Silva on his return to the attack. The last ball is tossed up on the stumps. Joshua blocks it.
Flighted fuller on middle and off, Joshua pushes it back to the bowler.
Flat on middle, Joshua blocks it.
This time outside off, Joshua Da Silva dabs it behind point and away from slip.
Short on middle, Joshua turns it to square leg but not in the gap.
Short on off, Joshua defends it off his back foot.
Change in bowling. Pace has been taken off as Dhananjaya de Silva is brought back on!
Flighted ball outside off and Rahkeem Cornwall pushes it with ease to mid off. Dot ball.
Darts this one in the line of the stumps and Rahkeem Cornwall, like always, is solid in his defence.
Flighted delivery on off, clipped away to mid-wicket by Rahkeem Cornwall.
Drifting on his pads, full ball and Rahkeem Cornwall blocks it out without any issues.
Full on his stumps as Joshua Da Silva clips it behind square leg for a run.
No ball! Another no ball from the spinner, this is poor. Darts one on the pads and Joshua Da Silva is hit on the pads as he misses his glance.
Drifts on his pads and Joshua Da Silva works across and clips it to short leg.
FOUR! The intent was clear! Calculated risk from Cornwall. Full on off, Cornwall sees there is no one at long off or closeby so he just leans and lofts his drive over that region for a boundary.
Length ball on off, Cornwall keeps it out.
Chipped over! Full on middle and off, Cornwall chips it over mid on and gets a brace as the fielder chases it and stops it before the ropes.
On the pads, Cornwall flicks but finds short mid-wicket.
Outside off, Cornwall leaves it alone.
50-run stand comes up! This partnership has put the hosts in a strong position after they found themselves in a tricky spot. Length ball around off, Joshua runs it down away from gully for one.
Flatter on off, Cornwall goes back and across to defend it back to the spinner.
Flatter, outside off, Rahkeem Cornwall thinks of going for the cut but abandons it in the end.
Full ball on the stumps, blocked out by Cornwall.
Nice and full on his stumps, Rahkeem Cornwall defends it from his crease.
Quicker, flatter on the stumps and played back to the bowler by Rahkeem Cornwall.

SIX! You bowl short to this man, you get punished. Lahiru Thirimanne drops this short on the stumps and Rahkeem Cornwall plays a handsome pull shot for a maximum over mid-wicket. The lead moves to 51!
Outside off and full. Joshua has no problems leaving that.
Full delivery on off, Joshua keeps it out.
On off, Joshua keeps it out.
Length ball outside off and swinging away. Joshua does not tease that one.

A huge and confident appeal for caught behind but it's turned down. It was just a bluff as Dimuth Karunaratne has decided not to review it either. Good length ball outside off, Joshua looks to defend it away from his body. He misses it though. Dickwella goes up in a confident appeal and his teammates follow him. The umpire though is unmoved.
FOUR! This one is for the highlight reel! Slightly overpitched on off, Joshua leans forward and drives it wonderfully through mid off for a boundary.
Floated this one on middle stump and it is blocked away by Rahkeem Cornwall.
Beaten! Fires a quicker one, on off. There is not enough width for Rahkeem Cornwall's attempted cut shot and he is beaten.
FOUR! Crunched away by Rahkeem Cornwall this time. Short and wide outside off, Rahkeem Cornwall rocks back and cuts it uppishly through to the point boundary.
Shortish ball again, Rahkeem Cornwall punches this nicely off the back foot to covers.
Drops his length this time and Rahkeem Cornwall continues with his solid defensive shots.
Flighted ball on middle, blocked out by Rahkeem Cornwall.
Around off, kept out by Joshua.
Full and wide outside off, Joshua leaves it alone.
Hits the deck hard outside off, Joshua defends it to covers.
Full on off, Joshua pushes it to covers.
Good length ball outside off, Joshua Da Silva leaves it alone.
Lakmal starts with a length ball on the pads, Rahkeem Cornwall flicks it to the leg side for one.
Suranga Lakmal is back on! He has been the star with the ball for Sri Lanka and already has five wickets to his name.
Flighted ball on off and the keeper-batsman is solid in his front foot defence.
Shortish ball on his stumps as Rahkeem Cornwall punches it down to long on for a run.
Shorter ball outside off, Rahkeem Cornwall punches it to covers.
Darts this one on his stumps and it is blocked away by Rahkeem Cornwall.
Drops this one short and Rahkeem Cornwall goes back in his crease to play it to covers.
Starts off with a loopy ball on the stumps, which is defended off the front foot by Rahkeem Cornwall.
Change in bowling. Lasith Embuldeniya is brought back into the attack.

Drinks break. A good passage of play for West Indies after losing a couple of wickets in a hurry. The pair of Joshua Da Silva and Rahkeem Cornwall has done well though for the home team to form a partnership and the lead is now stretched to 35 runs. Sri Lanka would not want this lead to get close to 100 and would be aiming to pick the remaining wickets as soon as possible. The second ball is at their service and let's see how they fare with the new nut.
Excellent delivery! Good length ball pitching outside off and it comes back in sharply. Joshua leaves it alone but plants his back foot on off stump. Luckily for him, it misses everything.
Solid defense! Fuller on off, Joshua gets on his front foot and defends it to cover.
Slash and a miss! Full and wide outside off. Joshua falls in the honey trap and goes for the drive. Luckily he does not edge it as he misses it completely.
Full outside off, Joshua leaves it alone.
Another well-timed shot! This one does not race away to the fence but gives him a couple. Full on off, Joshua drives it through point and gets a brace.

FOUR! Good shot and West Indies are changing gears! Brings up the 200 for the hosts! Good length ball outside off, Joshua Da Silva punches it nicely and down the ground through extra cover for a boundary.
SIX! He hits that with the wind and hits it well! Short ball on his body and Rahkeem Cornwall nails this pull shot over mid-wicket for a six.
Short of a length and pushed to mid on by Rahkeem Cornwall.
FOUR! Powerful, very powerful stroke. He bowls it very full on the stumps, the ball swings in a bit after pitching and Rahkeem Cornwall whips it to mid-wicket for a boundary.
Nahhh, wrong line this time. Bowls this wide outside off and Rahkeem Cornwall is not at all interested.
Drifts on his pads this time as Joshua Da Silva picks it to mid-wicket for a run. Easy pickings.
Good short ball to start off with the new ball. Short of a length, on his body as Joshua Da Silva keeps it out.
Change in bowling. Vishwa Fernando (15-5-41-0) is into the attack and is set to share the second new ball with Dushmantha Chameera.
Wrong line, drifting on his pads and Joshua Da Silva tucks it to mid-wicket to keep the strike.
Beaten! Seam movement and a bit of bounce too! Length ball, right on the fourth stump and whizzes past Joshua Da Silva's attempted defence.
Again, a bit wide of off stump and Joshua Da Silva shoulders his arms.
Length ball outside off and Joshua Da Silva is not interested in offering a shot.
Misses out on a poor delivery, does Joshua Da Silva. It is a wide and short ball, but it is cut straight to point.
Bit of shape away there. Length ball on off, seams away after pitching as Joshua Da Silva defends it well.
Sri Lanka have decided to take the second new ball now. Also, Suranga Lakmal is back on the field. He won't get a pop at the new cherry first up. It will be Dushmantha Chameera!
Drops his length this time and it is worked to mid-wicket by Joshua Da Silva.

Rapped on the pads but nothing from the umpire. Flighted ball on leg stump as Joshua Da Silva looks to defend it, he misses the shot and is hit on pads. Stifled appeal from Sri Lanka but the umpire is not interested.
Shortish ball on leg stump and it is tucked around by the keeper-batsman.
Flighted ball on off, played to covers.
In the air..but wide of short leg. Loopy ball on stumps, Rahkeem Cornwall jabs at it but gets an inside edge past short leg. They cross.
Darts this in the line of the stumps and Rahkeem Cornwall defends it off the front foot.
Second new ball available now. Will Sri Lanka opt for it straightaway or wait for a while? Lasith Embuldeniya is continuing with the old ball for the moment.
Well played Rahkeem Cornwall. Short of a length on off as he walks across to tuck it to square leg for a single.
Short delivery near his shoulders and it's defended with comfort to covers.
FOUR! Ahh, that was pleasant to watch. Bit overpitched on off and Rahkeem Cornwall hits it through the line past mid off for a boundary.
Fuller delivery this time, Rahkeem Cornwall walks across and plays it back to the bowler.
Another short ball, this one climbs higher but Rahkeem Cornwall is able to play it off the back foot.
Short of a length on off and Rahkeem Cornwall gets on his toes to defend it.
Flighted ball on off and a good defensive shot to finish the over.
Brings out the arm ball this time. In the line of the stumps, defended back to the bowler.
Darts this outside off and Joshua Da Silva is not interested in it, leaves it alone.
Nice flighted delivery on off and Joshua Da Silva is equally good in his defence.
Flighted ball down leg stump, Joshua Da Silva misses his flick.
Loopy ball on off and Joshua Da Silva defends it to short mid-wicket.
Surprises him with some short stuff, does Dushmantha Chameera. Bowls a bouncer on his body and Joshua Da Silva pulls it away to keep the strike.
Inside edge, just past the stumps! Joshua Da Silva looks to run this length ball behind the wickets but gets an inside edge to the keeper.
Fullish ball on off and Joshua Da Silva plays a high elbow shot back to the bowler.
Fires this full, at 142kmph at the stumps as Joshua Da Silva plays it back to the bowler.
A bit shorter this time, around fourth stump and the keeper batsman is solid in his front foot defence.
Fired full, in the line of the stumps and Joshua Da Silva negotiates it well.
Short around off, Cornwall looks to defend it off his back foot. He does so off the upper half of his bat. The ball dabs onto the crease and rolls behind but away from the stump.
Darted fuller, Cornwall pushes it back to the bowler.
Tossed up on off, Cornwall blocks it.
Flighted on off, RC keeps it out.
Floated on off, Cornwall defends it.
FOUR! Rahkeem Cornwall gets off the mark with a boundary! Short around off, Cornwall picks the length early and pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Good length ball outside off. Joshua shoulders arms to it.
On the pads, Cornwall looks to flick but misses. The ball hits his pad and goes to the leg side. He takes a single.
Outside off, RC watches it carry to the keeper.
Edged but does not carry! Good length delivery on off and shaping away. Conrwall looks to defend but gets an outside edge. Luckily for Rahkeem, it does not carry to first slip.
Good looking push for nothing. Full on off, Cornwall drives it to the right of short extra cover. The man there dives and denies him from getting off the mark.
Good length ball on off, Joshua taps it to cover and gets to the other end.
Lakmal is off the field for some break and he is being hauled off with applause by his teammates! Dushmantha Chameera is back on. 1/42 from 14 overs for him.
Flighted on off, Cornwall manages to see it off.
Embuldeniya gives this air on middle, Cornwall lunges forward and defends it.
On the pads, Joshua flicks it to square leg and gets to the other end.
Tossed up on the stumps, Da Silva keeps it out.
Floated on off, Joshua blocks it.
Flat and short on off, Joshua Da Silva pulls it but finds short mid-wicket.
Rahkeem Cornwall walks out to bat now.

OUT! CAUGHT! 5-wicket haul for Suranga Lakmal! This has been a phenomenal bowling display from the tall Sri Lankan pacer. Fullish ball outside off, Alzarri, who is more than capable with the bat, goes for the drive. The ball shapes away and his drive goes off the outer half of his bat. The ball goes low to the left of point. Dinesh Chandimal there reacts quickly and takes a very good catch.
Length delivery on off and shaping away. Alzarri Joseph defends it with the movement to point.
Good length ball outside off. Alzarri is aware of his off stump and leaves it alone.
On the pads, Joshua turns it to fine leg and rotates the strike.
Length ball on off, Joshua defends it to cover.
On the pads, Joshua flicks but finds short mid-wicket.
Review time, yet again! A shout of an lbw against Joseph is not entertained and Karunratne takes the DRS after having a word with his bowler. This one looks very close to the bat.

SAFE! An arm ball is served on middle, skidding in, Alzarri tries to defend it with his bat and pad together. They appeal for an lbw but the umpire feels that it's bat first and turns it down. Sri Lanka take the review. It's difficult to conclude whether it was bat first or pad, looked like that happened simultaneously, as shown by the Ultra Edge. The third umpire decides to go with the on-field decision as the replays are not conclusive. It stays not out. The Lankan skipper has a word with the umpire, he is not looking happy with the decision. Maybe, he wanted to know why Ball Tracker was not used further. Fair point. But it wouldn't have mattered anyway.
Goes flat and lands it on off, Joseph sticks on the back foot in defense.
Skidding down the leg side, Joshua nudges it behind square leg for a run. West Indies into the lead now.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Flatter and on middle, Da Silva gets opened up in defense as he blocks it out to the leg side.
Flatter and shorter around off, Joshua punches it to the left of the cover fielder, looks for a run but it's not on.
Slips the last delivery down the leg side, Joseph allows it through to the keeper. End of a successful over!
A length ball on off, angling in, Joseph defends it near his front pad.
Good length delivery outside off, Joseph plays inside the line and blocks it down.
Alzarri Joseph is the new batsman with the scores level.

OUT! STUMPS SHATTERED! Lakmal has four in the match now and he is ecstatic. Once again he dishes out a delivery that nips back in after landing on a length outside off, Holder tries his best to defend with a straight bat but it brushes the toe half of his bat, possibly clips some part of his pads and deflects behind to uproot the off stump. This is top class bowling from Suranga Lakmal.

Speedy delivery, skidding into the batsman after landing on a good length around middle, Holder tries his best to work it away on the leg side but misses. He takes a blow on his pads but it's too high.
Fuller and close to off, Holder defends it from the front foot to the off side.
Fullish and on middle, knocked down to mid on.
Called a no ball! Full and flighted on off, Joshua defends it off his front foot. Embuldeniya is just walking into his delivery stride but still overstepped. Strange! Scores level now.
Goes flatter this time and serves it on middle, Holder moves back and turns it to square leg where the fielder misfields and allows a run.
Gem of a delivery! Lasith Embuldeniya slows it up in the air and pitches it full around off, Holder tries to defend the original line but it spins away to beat the outside edge.
Lasith drags his length short and delivers it on middle, Joshua quickly goes on the back foot and works it to mid-wicket for a run.
Loopy and full on off, Da Silva dead-bats it to the off side.
Flatter and on off, Joshua has just blocked that from his crease.
Spin from the other end.
A length delivery in the zone outside off, Holder is forward as he defends it to the off side.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.

DRS time! Huge shout for an lbw and the umpire stays unmoved. Suranga Lakmal manages to convince his skipper and they take the referral. No bat involved, confirms Ultra Edge. Ball Tracker shows that the impact is in line but it's heading over the stumps.

NOT OUT! Holder is safe! Brilliant delivery by Lakmal yet again. He lets out a good length ball on off which nips back in to beat the defensive bat of Holder and strikes him on the back leg. The Sri Lankan players appeal in unison but it's not given by the umpire. Dimuth Karunaratne goes for the referral after consulting his players but the Ball Tracker shows it to be going over the stumps. A review lost for the touring team.

Oooh...that was close to the off stump! Lakmal uses the crease well and angles in a good length ball on off, this time it skids on with the angle rather than going away off the seam. Holder shoulders arms and it goes over the off stump.
This time the Lankan speedster delivers it full and in the channel outside off, a hint of away shape there, Holder stays back to covers his stumps and then allows it through.
Lakmal begins his spell by angling in a length ball close to off, Holder stays on the back foot as he offers a straight bat in defense.
Suranga Lakmal returns for another burst. Three slips and a gully waiting.

Finds the gap this time Joshua Da Silva. Fullish ball on the fifth stump and Joshua Da Silva gets an outside edge through the slips and down to third man for a couple of runs. The fielder collects it millimeters in front off the boundary rope and the umpires go upstairs to check whether it was a four. The replay shows that it was very close to the boundary and in the end it is decided that is just a couple of runs.
Full ball on off and Joshua Da Silva leans in and plays a solid front foot defence.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
A bit of movement back in for Dushmantha Chameera. Bowls it on a length and gets it to nip back in as Joshua Da Silva works it to square leg. Dot ball.
Straying down his pads, Joshua Da Silva looks to flick it but the ball is way down the leg side.
Right there in the corridor of uncertainty. Da Silva is glued to his crease and plays it to gully.
Who will start the session from the other end? It will be Dushmantha Chameera!

Edged but safe! First run of the final session of the day. Floated on middle, Joshua Da Silva gets on his front foot to defend but the ball takes the inside edge and lobs over the vacant leg slip region. They take a run.
Floated on off, Joshua blocks it.
On the stumps, kept out.
Tossed up on off, Joshua blocks it.
Floated on leg, Da Silva keeps it out.
Dhananjaya de Silva starts with a shorter ball on middle, Joshua resumes with a solid back foot defense.

We are back for the final session of the day! Joshua Da Silva and Jason Holder stride out to resume their innings. The Sri Lankan players are already out on the field. Dhananjaya de Silva to start the session with the ball.
... Day 2, Evening session ...

Once again Suranga Lakmal and Dushmantha Chameera impressed with their performance. They shared all the wickets to fall in the afternoon and looked quite threatening. Kyle Mayers' counter-punch offered West Indies some brisk runs and the ongoing stand has helped them to narrow the deficit. Plenty to look forward to in the final session. Do join us at 1500 local (1900 GMT).

91/3 in 30 overs! An eventful session of Test cricket. Sri Lanka will be pleased with their progress in this Test match but with West Indies now just 6 runs behind and still having five wickets in the bank will bother them slightly. It's a good pitch for batting, no doubt, but still, as a bowler, you are getting some purchase every now and then. Keeping that in mind, the Lankans won't want to concede a big lead here. For West Indies, it's all about swelling this lead and bat for as long as possible.
Joshua Da Silva to start proceedings post Tea.

Beaten! Good delivery to end the session and to go into Tea. Bowls this at a length, outside off, Holder was stuck in his crease as he tries to defend it off the front foot. The ball goes past the outside edge. That is Tea, with West Indies at 163 with half their side back in the shed.
Full ball on his pads and Holder plays it uppishly, but on the bounce to mid on.
Plays it with soft hands and gets a couple here. Full ball outside off and Jason Holder gently nudges this past point for a couple
He is getting the ball to shape back in here. Fires it on a length outside off and it nips back in sharply as Joshua Da Silva works it past mid-wicket for a run.
In the air...but short. Full ball onto the pads and Jason Holder picks it on the leg side. The ball drops short of deep square leg and they cross over.
Straying down the leg stump and misses Holder's flick shot.
Now calmly defends this back of a length ball to see off the over. Good batting from Joshua Da Silva!
Dushmantha Chameera comes into the attack.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Vishwa looks to go for the yorker but serves a crispy full toss wide outside off. Joshua Da Silva drives it through point and gets a boundary. Brings down the deficit to 10 now.
Good length ball outside off, Joshua looks to play it behind point but the ball zips a little extra and stings the upper part and glove of Da Silva and goes to gully.
Length delivery on off, Joshua Da Silva keeps it out.
Full outside off, Joshua Da Silva drives but the man at point runs to his left and puts a dive to keep it down to a dot. Just the kind of effort Sri Lanka need on the field.
Length ball on off, Joshua Da Silva keeps it out.
Slower and wide outside off, Jason Holder thinks of playing it at first but lets it go in the end.
Full ball on off as Jason Holder defends it off the front foot.
Slower through the air, outside off and defended with comfort by the big man.
Purchase for the spinner! He bowls this a bit short and gets the ball to turn. Joshua Da Silva goes back in his crease to defend it but gets the outside edge through slips for a run.
Flighted ball and defended off the front foot by Joshua Da Silva.
Flatter ball on off and defended with ease.
FOUR! Holder at his best! Good length ball wide outside off, Holder punches it through covers and gets a boundary. Reduces the deficit to just 15 now.
Full on middle, Holder pushes it to mid off.
Good length ball around off, Holder is happy to block it.
Yorker on off, Holder jams it out.
Length ball on middle, Holder turns it but finds short mid-wicket.
Full on middle, Jason defends it.
Flighted on off and defended back to the bowler.
Good delivery. Flighted on off and Joshua Da Silva plays a solid front foot defence.
A very full ball on the pads and Joshua Da Silva sweeps it to long leg for a couple.
Flighted ball on the stumps and the keeper-batsman pushes it back to the bowler.
Loopy ball on off and Jason Holder works it down to long off for a run.
Flighted ball on off, Jason leans into it and defends it to covers.
Ful on middle and leg, Joshua Da Silva flicks it through square leg and gets a couple.

On the pads, Holder looks to flick but misses. The ball kisses the thigh pad and goes to the left of the keeper. Niroshan Dickwella dives and gets his gloves to it but cannot hold onto it cleanly. The ball goes towards short fine leg and they take a run.
Full on middle, Holder defends it.
On off, kept out.

FOUR OVERTHROWS! Joshua Da Silva apologizes but Holder is happy as he has got four free runs. Length ball on middle, Holder tucks it to the leg side. Joshua comes out for a run but Holder says no. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end. The ball hits Joshua's bat and deflects to the long off fence. Joshua Da Silva raises his hand in apology and this reminds us of the 2019 World Cup final to that iconic moment.
Good shot! Full on off, Holder pushes it right off the middle through covers and gets a couple.
A solid front foot defensive shot by Joshua Da Silva to finish this over.
Flighted ball on middle and it is flicked away to short mid-wicket.
Tosses this one outside off and Joshua Da Silva defends it nicely to covers.
Loopy ball on off and once again defended by Joshua Da Silva.
Loopy ball on middle and Joshua Da Silva puts in a good stride to defend it.
Flighted ball on leg stumps and defended with ease.
This is well down leg and too high. On the pads, Holder looks to flick but misses and gets hit high on the thigh pad. Vishwa goes up in appeal but without much support.
On middle and off, Holder keeps it out.

NOT OUT! Umpire's call saves Jason Holder. Unlucky for Vishwa Fernando but a lucky escape for Jason Holder! Good length delivery pitching outside off. It jags back in a lot. Holder looks to play but misses due to the inward movement.  The ball hits the pad and a huge appeal follows. The umpire though is unmoved.  Dimuth Karunaratne signals the 'T' and takes it upstairs. Replay rolls in and it shows day-light between bat and ball so the third umpire moves to Ball Tracker. The Ball Tracker rolls in and it shows that the ball is clipping the stumps and it's the umpire's call. Not enough to reverse the on-field decision. Big scare for West Indies and Holder but they survive. Sri Lanka do not lose their review but do not get their man either.
Review time! LBW appeal turned down by the umpire but Dimuth Karunaratne has decided to send it upstairs. Let's see what the replays have to say.
Full and on off, pushed back by Holder.
Good length, on off and defended with ease.
Joshua is off the mark with an inside edge to square leg off a full delivery on off.
Vishwa Fernando to have a crack at the Windies now.
A solid front foot defense from Holder to see off the over.
Tossed up on middle, Holder lunges forward and blocks it.
Floated on off, Holder keeps it out.

FOUR! Breaking the shackles! There was some risk in the shot but Holder threw caution out of the window there. Floated on middle and off, Holder goes over mid on and gets enough bat on it to send it over the fielder there and get a boundary.
Tossed up on middle, Holder keeps it out.
On the stumps, kept out.
Length ball on off, the new man Joshua Da Silva prods forward to defend it but gets an inside edge to square leg. Wicket maiden for Suranga Lakmal.
Full ball on off and he defends it with ease.
In the channel outside off, Joshua offers no shot.
Full ball on middle and defended off the front foot.
Good delivery first up. Length ball, swinging away after pitching and Joshua Da Silva defends it off the front foot.
Joshua Da Silva is the new man in for West Indies.

OUT! CAUGHT IN SLIPS! This is outstanding bowling by Suranga Lakmal, pure brilliance. Comes round the wicket, bowls it at a length, and gets enough movement to force an outside edge to Dhananjaya de Silva at second slip. No real foot movement by Kyle Mayers while looking to drive it and that's what cost him his wicket. Kyle Mayers was looking good out in the middle and his wicket will put pressure on the West Indies.
Flighted outside off, Holder keeps it out.
This time Mayers punches it to sweeper cover and gets a single.
Nice stroke for nothing. Short around off, Mayers punches it but finds short extra cover.
Flat around off, KM keeps it out.
Short outside off, Mayers looks to punch but misses. Niroshan Dickwella behind the stumps fails to gather it cleanly.
Short outside off, Mayers punches it to mid off.
Good delivery to finish a testing over for the West Indies. Full, fast and on off as Jason Holder moves across to defend it.
Length ball on off, Kyle Mayers gets an inside edge to square leg for a run.
Geez this is some good bowling from Suranga Lakmal. He fires this one fast, on the pads and Kyle Mayers is again rapped on the pads as he misses his flick.
Under edge this time. Short and outside off, Kyle Mayers looks to cut it away but gets the under edge to the keeper.
Length ball, on off and hits Kyle Mayers on the pads as he once again misses his glance.
This one skids off the surface. Coming round the wicket, Kyle fires it on a length on off and it hits Kyle Mayers high on the thigh pad as he misses the glance.
Shorter on off, Holder punches it to the left of the bowler. Embuldeniya manages to get to it and saves runs for his side.
Tossed up on off, Holder keeps it out.
Floated on off, Holder blocks it.

NOT OUT! Holder gets his back leg back inside the crease. Flighted delivery outside off, Holder looks to go over mid off but the ball turns and beats the outside edge and goes past the off stump. Dickwella is quick to take the bails off and the slip fielder appeals. It's referred upstairs but one replay is enough to confirm that Jason is safe.
A stumping appeal is taken upstairs. Was Holder's back leg outside the crease or in the air? Or was he in?
Flighted outside off, Holder leaves it alone.
Short outside off, Mayers punches it to deep point for one.
Lasith Embuldeniya to bowl now.
Fullish ball on off, the big man walks across and defends it to point.
A little straighter, on his pads and clipped away to the leg side.
Beaten! Peach by Suranga Lakmal. Hits the deck hard and bowls it on a length outside off, the ball nips away a bit and whizzes past Holder's defensive attempt.
Right length and line by Suranga Lakmal. On a length on the fourth stump, defended with ease.
Length ball but this is wide outside off and Holder lets it go.
Fires one on a length in the line of his stumps, Jason Holder plays it to square leg. He wanted the run but was sent back by Kyle Mayers.

Drinks break. Sri Lanka have done a superb job in the last hour by picking up a couple of wickets but at the same time, they have conceded 58 runs as well. They cannot afford to relax as the deficit is now down to 39 and that's mainly due to the counter-attacking knock by Kyle Mayers. Once again the pitch has gifted something to the bowlers and the Lankans would hope to use that to their advantage and run through the West Indian batting line-up. A crucial hour coming up after the mini-break.
FOUR! Mayers enters into the 40s! Just a bit of width on offer outside off, the length is slightly on the shorter side, Kyle camps back and whacks it through backward point for a boundary.
Flashes and misses! Short and wide outside off, Mayers decides to go after it, throws his bat but fails to connect.
A length ball just outside off, skidding on after landing, Mayers covers his stumps and allows it through.
A tempter outside off, full in length and there to be driven, Kyle chooses to leave it.

FOUR! Muscled! Kyle Mayers speeds along to 38, five fours and two sixes in his knock so far. He picks the length early which is on the shorter side and blazes it away via a pull shot to the deep mid-wicket fence.
Shortish and outside off, punched through cover-point for a couple of runs.
Good length ball on off, straightening just a bit, Holder leaves and it heads over the off pole. Terrific over by Lakmal, a wicket maiden.
Angles in a good length ball on off, Holder defends it from the back foot.
Movement in the air and off the surface, a length ball outside off, the batsman lets the ball go outside his leg stump.

Good length ball on off, shaping away a bit, Holder pushes at it and gets it away off the outer half of his bat. It rolls wide of gully, there is confusion over a run but Holder decides against it eventually.
Fullish and outside off, Holder slices his attempted drive towards cover-point.
Jason Holder walks in next.

OUT! Cleaned him up! Lakmal returns and creates an impact straightaway. That's too loose from Blackwood. Lakmal serves a fuller length ball close to off and gets it to skid off the surface. Jermaine decides to have a drive through the line but it keeps coming in with the angle, grabs the inside edge and cannons onto the stumps behind. Lakmal has been superb all day with his outswingers but gets a wicket this time with an incomer!
Double bowling change from Sri Lanka. Suranga Lakmal to have his first go in the afternoon session. 14-4-31-1 are his figures thus far.
Spears in a full ball on off, Kyle stays back to this delivery too and pushes it out safely to covers. 9 from the over and the deficit for West Indies is under 50.

FOUR! No half measures this time! Kyle Mayers is ready to play his shots and he is dealing in boundaries at the moment. Short and around off, Mayers picks the length early and muscles his pull shot off the front foot. Fantastic connection and it goes over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Good length delivery outside off, Kyle sticks back to play it down towards cover-point.

FOUR! A fortunate boundary for Kyle Mayers. A touch short in length delivery around off, Mayers swivels on the back foot with the pull shot and inside edges it past the stumps to fine leg for a boundary. On another day, he would have dragged it on!
Stays back to a length ball and keeps it out safely to the off side.
Fernando chooses to operate from 'round the wicket to the right-hander and angles in a good length ball on off, Blackwood glances it behind square leg and gathers a single.
Change of bowler. Vishwa Fernando replaces Dushmantha Chameera from this end. 9-5-5-0 are his figures so far. Very frugal.
Loopy and full on off, Mayers drives it firmly back to the bowler.

FOUR! Brilliant use of the crease by Kyle Mayers. A touch short in length on middle, Mayers immediately drops his weight on the back leg, goes deep inside the crease and muscles it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Quicker one on middle, fuller in length, Mayers draws forward in defense but once again it skids off the surface, catches the inside edge and raps him on the pads.
A slider, full and around off, skidding back in, Mayers tries to unfurl an off drive but it takes the inside half and rolls on the leg side.
Quicker and fuller around off, Mayers defends it near his front pad.
Very full in length on middle, Blackwood drives it down to deepish mid on and opens his account with a single.

FOUR! Sweetly driven! Elegant and graceful. Slightly overpitched and around off, Kyle Mayers bends his back knee as he transfers his weight into the drive and thumps it through covers for a glorious boundary.
Back of a length ball on off, Mayers sticks back, allows the ball to come to him and plays it nice and late towards point. Would have loved to find the gap there.

Mixing his length superbly, Chameera. The follow-up delivery is full and outside off, Kyle goes nowhere with his footwork, probably expecting another bouncer, and leaves it by staying on the back foot.
Terrific bouncer by Chameera. Catches the batsman by surprise. It's bowled on middle and leg, Mayers picks it late but still does well to evade it.
This time Chameera bowls it on a good length outside off and his natural angle takes the ball into the batsman, Kyle guards his stumps and shoulders arms.
Fuller length delivery in the zone outside off, holding its line, Kyle allows it through to the keeper.
Mishit! A shortish ball has been fired on middle, Mayers fails to control his horizontal-batted shot and it takes the top half of his blade. It lands safely behind square leg and they take a run.
Dhananjaya gives this delivery some extra airtime and lands it full outside off, Mayers takes a big stride forward to cover the line and then leaves it alone.
The off spinner is once again on the shorter side outside off, Mayers cuts but finds the point fielder.
Dhananjaya goes flat and short around off, Mayers hangs on the back foot and punches it to mid on.

SIX! Enough of blocking, Mayers decides to go aerial and dispatches it over the bowler's head. Full and flighted on middle, a little bit of shimmy down the track by Kyle and he sends it packing over the fence. 100 comes up for West Indies!
Loopy and full around off, Mayers strides forward and defends it with his bat and pad together.
Chameera goes wide of the crease and arrows in a good length ball outside off, Blackwood does well to deal with the extra bounce as he defends it to covers. End of a successful over for Chameera.
Good length delivery close to off, Jermaine goes on the back foot and defends it to the off side.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Full ball on off and defended off the front foot.
Jermaine Blackwood has arrived in the middle.

OUT! Caught behind! Beautiful piece of bowling by Chameera and he finally has a wicket to his name in this innings. He speeds in from 'round the wicket and hurls in a good length ball close to off, Campbell is forced to play the trajectory but the ball straightens off the seam after hitting the deck and there is some extra bounce too. As a result, the outside edge is induced and Dickwella makes no mistake behind the stumps. The 148-ball fight from John is over. West Indies trail by 74 runs!
Fullish ball around off, Campbell drives it square of the wicket on the off side and collects a couple of runs.

Beauty of a delivery! Tossed up ball landing close to off, Kyle goes on the back foot to deal with it but it straightens a touch to beat the outside edge and goes over the off stump. Extra bounce saved Mayers.
Slows this up in the air and lands it full on off, Kyle draws forward to meet the ball and jams it out.
Fires this one quick and flat in the line of the off stump, Mayers does well to have his bat down in defense.
Dhananjaya goes short and wide outside off, Mayers mistimes his back foot punch to covers.
Gives this one some extra air and lands it full around off, Kyle presses forward and defends it to covers.
Begins his over with a flatter shorter ball on off, Mayers gets back and punches it down to mid on.
Wide outside off this time, John Campbell lets it be.
Beaten! The ball comes in with the angle as he bowling from round the wicket, pitches on off and shapes away a bit to beat John Campbell's defence.
Full ball on stumps and he defends it from the crease.
Leg bye! Length ball on the pads, Kyle Mayers looks to defend it but gets hit on the pad. The ball goes down to third man and they cross over.
SIX! First six of the innings and it is off the bat of Kyle Mayers. Dushmantha Chameera bowls this short and on his body and Kyle Mayers hooks it over square leg for a maximum.
Misses the cut shot this time. Short and wide outside off and Kyle Mayers attempts a cut shot but is beaten.
Short and spinning away from John Campbell. He initially looks to punch but opts against it.
Floated on middle, Campbell pushes it to the left of the bowler. Dhananjaya de Silva dives and saves runs.
Good running! These two are taking quick singles in this session but none with risk. Short on off, Mayers punches it to the right of cover and takes a run.
Darted fuller and quicker around off. Mayers pushes it to point.
Flighted around off, Mayers defends it to cover.
Another single. Loopy ball on off, Campbell pushes it ti mid off and takes a quick run.
Wrong line this time by Dushmantha Chameera. He bowls it at a length but wide outside off as Kyle Mayers lets it go.
Short ball on his body and John Campbell pulls it to square leg to cross over for a single.
Fullish ball on off and defended to short mid off.
Good length ball, but this is wide outside off. It goes way past the batter's defence.
Fullish ball, outside off and John Campbell leans into it to hit it to covers.
Full ball, outside off and John Campbell mimics an off drive after letting the ball go.
Change in bowling. First one of the session and it sees Dushmantha Chameera being recalled into the attack. He replaces Lasith Embuldeniya! 0/23 from Dushmantha Chameera's 8 overs so far.
Slightly short on middle and off. Kyle defends it off his back foot. 5 overs of the post Lunch session is done and Sri Lanka yet to bowl a maiden.
Darted outside off, it is the arm ball. Mayers picks it and leaves it alone.
Tossed up on off, Mayers once again defends it.
Flighted on off, Mayers gets on his front foot and defends it.
Darted fuller on middle. The man at mid on is standing a bit deep. Campbell plays it to him and gets a single.
Floated outside off, Campbell sweeps it fine to the leg side and gets a couple as the fielder at deep mid-wicket cleans it up.

In the air...but safe! Short ball outside off, there is an extra bit of bounce as John Campbell looks to pull it away. He gets the top edge but it lands in no man's land in the fine leg region. Single taken.
Misses out on that one, does John Campbell. Short ball, outside off. John Campbell goes back into his crease and hits the pull shot straight to backward square leg.
Full ball on the stumps, defended with ease.
Short ball in the line of the stumps and the batsman defends it.
Flatter ball on middle and played from the crease by John.
John Campbell goes back and across to defend this ball.
Darted on off, KM blocks it to see off the over.
Floated on off, Mayers keeps it out.
Flighted on off, Mayers keeps it out. Niroshan Dickwella likes it from behind the stumps as he can be heard saying 'good Danny, good Danny'.
Slightly shorter on off, Campbell knocks it to mid off for one.
On the pads, Campbell tucks it away from short leg.
Floated outside off, Campbell shoulders arms to this.
Beaten! Beautiful delivery by Lasith Embuldeniya. Slower through the air, Kyle Mayers goes for the booming drive but is beaten.
Flighted ball outside off and Kyle Mayers plays a solid front foot defence to point.
Loopy ball on his stumps, John Campbell comes down the track and plays it to long on for a run.
Quicker ball on the stumps, defended back to the bowler.
Flatter ball on the stumps and worked to short mid-wicket.
FOUR! Tremendous by John Campbell. Comes down to the pitch of the ball and smacks it past short mid off for a boundary.
Who will start the session from the other end? It will be spin from both ends as Lasith Embuldeniya will share the opposite end with Dhananjaya de Silva!

Dangerous leave to end the first over of the session. Tossed up outside off, Mayers shoulders arms to this. The ball does not turn and keeps straight. Luckily for Mayers, he was aware of his off pole. As they say, any leave that misses the stump is a good leave.
Floated on off, Mayers keeps it out.
First run of the session! Campbell comes down the track and plays it to the right of mid off. The fielder there dives and saves runs for his side.
On the pads, Campbell turns it to the leg side.
Floated on off, Campbell defends it to extra cover.
Spin and bounce for Dhananjaya! Flighted outside off, it is slightly short. Campbell looks to sweep but the turn and bounce see him play that shot half-heartedly.

We are all set for the action to begin! The Sri Lankan players are out on the field. John Campbell and Kyle Mayers walk out to the middle to resume their innings. Dhananjaya de Silva is ready to start the session with the ball.
... Day 2, Afternoon session ...

We are expecting more of the same from both teams in the afternoon as well. John Campbell seems to be given the role of an anchor around whom the rest of the West Indian batting will revolve. There is not much pressure on them at the moment but maintaining a low run rate might hurt them if they start to lose wickets at regular intervals. For Sri Lanka, it's all about bowling disciplined lines and keeping things tight. The pitch is offering something to their spinners as well and the likes of Lasith Embuldeniya and Dhananjaya de Silva could be seen doing the bulk of the bowling after the break. Do join us at 1240 local (1640 GMT) for the second session.

Suranga Lakmal and Dushmantha Chameera were the most impressive bowlers for the Lankans. The latter even succeeded in dismissing Nkrumah Bonner earlier but it turned out to be a no ball. Speaking of Bonner, he survived a run out as well but eventually was trapped in front by Embuldeniya minutes before Lunch. John Campbell though has been very watchful, as always, and made some 'lightsaber' leaves. The hosts would be feeling that they lost one wicket too many in this session. Still, they have the upper hand and would try to show more intent in the next session.

A session of attritional cricket comes to a close! Sri Lanka tried hard throughout the morning session and the second wicket just before the break would make them a lot happier. Their lines and lengths were nicely assisted by some movement off the surface but the visiting team failed to utilize it to the fullest. Despite bowling so well, they remain on the back foot as West Indies have brought the deficit under 100 courtesy of the 56-run stand between Campbell and Bonner.
Shorter ball on middle and the new man in plays a solid back foot defence. That will be Lunch with West Indies at 72 for 2!
Kyle goes deep into his crease and punches it to covers.
Just wide of slip! Shorter ball outside off, Kyle Mayers goes deep in his crease and guides it past first slip for a couple. Off the mark.
Flatter delivery outside off, turns in and hits him on the pads as Kyle fails to defend.
Flatter ball on off, defended off the back foot.
No ball! Full ball on off and defended off the front foot. The replay shows that it was a front foot no ball.
Kyle Mayers walks out to bat in a tricky period as only a few minutes remain before we head for Lunch!

OUT! LBW! Umpire's call not just on hitting the wickets but also on impact. West Indies do not lose the review but it is not good enough to save Nkrumah Bonner! Short on off, Bonner plays a very casual shot. He looks to pull this one but misses as this one keeps straight with a hint of turn. He misses his pull and gets hit on the back pad. The Sri Lankan players put in a huge appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Bonner signals the 'T' straightaway. The Ultra Edge takes a lot of time to roll in but then eventually it does. Ultra Edge shows no spike involved. Time for the Ball Tracker. This rolls quickly. It shows that the pitching is fine. The impact though is on the line, i.e. Umpire's call. Further, it shows the ball to be clipping the off pole. Once again, the infamous Umpire's Call on impact. Bonner has to walk back and Sri Lanka will have at least two wickets before they head for Lunch.
Review time! Nkrumah Bonner has been adjudged LBW but he has straightaway reviewed it. This usually suggests that the batter has got some bat on it. Let's see what the replays have to say.
A solid front foot defense from Campbell to end the over. Just a single off Dhananjaya de Silva's first.
Flighted on off, JC keeps it out.
Shorter on middle, Campbell defends it against the stumps to the on side of the pitch.
Tossed up fuller on off, Campbell lunges forward and defends it onto the ground.
Good ball from de Silva! Floated fuller on off, Campbell goes on his front foot and blocks it.
Dhananjaya de Silva starts with a shorter delivery on middle. Bonner goes on his back foot and knocks it behind square leg for one.
Change in bowling. Dhananjaya de Silva is into the action for the first time in this game with the ball.
Strays down his pads and John Campbell works it towards fine leg region for a couple.
Loopy ball on off and defended with ease.
John Campbell goes back and across to defend this flatter ball outside off.
Flatter ball on off, defended easily again.

Edgy runs for Nkrumah Bonner. It is a short ball, outside off and Nkrumah Bonner looks to cut it away, he gets a thick outside edge and the ball goes down to third man. They run three before the fielder cuts it off.
Flatter ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Length delivery outside off, Campbell lets it carry to the keeper.
Short ball on middle, Campbell ducks under it.
Length ball on middle, Campbell tucks it with soft hands to short mid-wicket.
Good length ball outside off, Campbell shows his flair as he leaves this alone.

FOUR! Fifty runs stand is up in style! Full toss and wide outside off, Campbell is quick to lash onto it. He cuts it behind point and the ball races away to the fence. Just the third boundary of the innings for Campbell.
Full and wide outside off. Campbell offers a lightsaber leave to this one.
Flighted ball outside off, turns away after pitching and Nkrumah Bonner is not interested in offering a shot. Maiden over.

Brings out the arm ball on this occasion. Fires this one on off, it comes in with the angle as he is bowling from over the wicket. Nkrumah Bonner gets an inside edge onto his pads as he looks to defend.
Shortish ball on middle and Nkrumah Bonner defends it off the back foot.
Loppy ball on off as Nkrumah Bonner plays a solid front foot defence.
A bit outside off this time, Nkrumah Bonner lets it go.
Flatter ball on off, Nkrumah Bonner cuts it with the turn to point.
Short, around the body, Bonner hooks it to fine leg and keeps the strike. 10 off the over.

Lucky for Bonner that this does not hit the stumps. Good length ball on off. It comes back into the right-hander. Bonner looks to defend and does so off the inner half of his bat. The ball bounces, hits his hips and fortunately for the West Indies batter, it deflects off his right shoe, away from the stumps.

EDGED AND FOUR! Not in control this time! Another bouncer from Chameera. This is closer to the body. Bonner looks to pull but gets a top edge which goes fine down the leg side and crosses the fine leg fence.
NO BALL! Chameera oversteps again. This time he does not get a wicket off the illegal delivery. This is full on middle and off, Bonner defends it.

FOUR! Fifty comes up for West Indies with that boundary! Bouncer from Chameera. It is on off, Bonner pulls it in front of square on the leg side off his front foot and gets a boundary. Nicely played by Nkrumah Bonner!

Well fielded! Length ball outside off, Bonner waits for it and opens the face of the bat. He looks to run it down away from the man at gully but the fielder there dives to his left and saves runs for his side.
Length delivery on off, Bonner defends it.
Flatter delivery outside off to finish the over. It is defended off the back foot by John Campbell.
A bit of purchase for the spinner there! Flatter ball on off and turns back in as John Campbell defends it off the back foot.
Slower through the air, on middle and John Campbell comes down the track to defend it.
Flatter ball outside off and JC defends it off the back foot.

The physio is out now to have a look. Hopefully, Oshada Fernando is fine to continue and the damage is not a serious one. After a little bit of treatment and Oshada is back on his feet. Still holding the shoulder though as he gets ready to resume his duty at short leg. Tough boy!

Oh man, that must have hurt and the fielder at short leg is down in extreme pain. Lasith Embuldeniya drops this a bit short and John Campbell is quick to rock on his back foot and pull it. He middles it but hits it straight to short leg. It hits Oshada Fernando's shoulder who goes down in pain.
Starts with a flighted ball on the stumps as John Campbell comes down the wicket to defend it.
Change in bowling. Spin into the attack for the first time today! Lasith Embuldeniya is introduced into the attack. Just a solitary over from him so far.
Another solid block. This time the ball is on middle. Nkrumah keeps it out.
Good length delivery outside off. Bonner is happy to shoulder arms to it.
Effort ball from Dushmantha Chameera! He bangs it short around off, Bonner sways away from it.
Full on off, Campbell pushes it to mid off and gets a single.
Length ball on off, Campbell keeps it out.
Good length ball on middle, Campbell tucks it to the leg side.

Tell you what, a direct hit and Nkrumah was a goner. Full ball on off as John Campbell taps it to covers, there is a bit of hesitation between the two but they decide to take the quick run in the end. The fielder runs in and has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Replay shows that Nkrumah Bonner was short of his crease and would have been out in case of a direct hit. Another escape for Bonner.
No ball! Full ball outside off, it goes way past his front foot defence. Replay shows that Suranga Lakmal had overstepped. He will have to bowl it again.
Beaten! Beautiful channels by Lakmal. Back of a length, outside off and the ball whizzes past John Campbell's back foot defence.
Short and wide and it's left alone.
Leg bye. A short of length ball, comes back in after pitching and Nkrumah Bonner is rapped on his pads as he misses his glance. The ball rolls to square leg and they cross over.
Very full this time, almost a yorker on his stumps and Nkrumah Bonner punches it to short mid on.
Full ball, a touch outside off. Nkrumah Bonner plays a textbook front foot defence.
Dot and another fancy leave to end the over. Length ball outside off, Campbell leaves it in the 'Steven Smith style'. Everyone seems to be copying Smudge's peculiar habit these days.
Chameera bangs it short on off and middle. Campbell hops and tucks it to the leg side.
Good length ball outside off. John leaves it alone.
Full and wide outside off. A hint of Marnus Labuschagne and Steven Smith as Campbell leaves it in a fancy manner.
Chameera hits the deck hard on off. Bonner taps it to covers and takes an easy run.
Length ball on off, Bonner defends it.
Full and fast delivery on off, John Campbell defends it to short mid on. Excellent over by Lakmal, bowled it in the right channels.
Very good ball, right there in the corridor of uncertainty. John Campbell has been out there for a long time and lets this go.
Short of a length, nips back a bit after pitching outside off as John Campbell punches it to cover-point.
Length ball but this is wide outside off, it goes way past John Campbell's front foot defence.
Fullish, in the line of the stumps and John Campbell leans into it to play to short mid off.
Round the wicket, length ball outside off and John Campbell shoulders his arms.

Drinks break! A fantastic first hour or so of Test cricket. The Lankan pacers have been right on the money and there is some assistance for them from the pitch. They have got the prized scalp of Kraigg Brathwaite and should have got Nkrumah Bonner too had Dushmantha Chameera not overstepped in the last over. Despite bowling superbly, the visitors cannot afford such lapses. The early morning conditions might evaporate soon and then run-scoring will get easy. West Indies would be hoping to capitalize then.
Length ball on off, Bonner keeps it out.

Going down! Fullish ball, pitching on middle and leg and swinging in. Bonner looks to defend but misses and gets hit on the pad. There is a stifled appeal but the umpire is unmoved. Sri Lanka too do not go for the review.
Fuller on off, Bonner keeps it out.

Superb ball! Full outside off, tempting Bonner to have a go at that. He obliges and goes for a drive but misses it as the ball shapes away from him and beats the outside edge of his willow by a whisker.
Length ball on off, Bonner defends it to covers.

OUT! CAUGHT! NO! It's a NO BALL! A massive lifeline for Nkrumah Bonner! Brilliant delivery, a sharp catch but all for it to count for nothing as Chameera has done the big error of overstepping his line.  Good length ball pitching on middle and off. Bonner looks to defend but the ball shapes away and catches the outside edge of his willow. It goes quickly to the man at third slip. Pathum Nissanka there takes a sharp catch. The Lankan players are celebrating but the umpire gets the message from upstairs and he calls no ball.
Oh no! Oh my! Chameera has got the better of Bonner but only for it to be a no ball!
Good ball! Fullish and shaping away. Bonner looks to play it but misses.
He is getting the ball to nip back in sharply to the left-hander. Full ball, it pitches on off and jags back in. John Campbell defends it to short mid-wicket. A dot ball to finish a very good over.
Full, on off and John Campbell plays it right under his eyes, shouts 'NO' after playing the shot.
Quick single, good batting. Full outside off and Nkrumah Bonner nudges it to point for a run. Good running between the wickets.
Fullish ball on off, swings away after pitching and Bonner shoulders his arms.

Inswing and John Campbell does well to play it out. It pitches on off and nips back in sharply, John Campbell looks to play it down the ground but gets it off the inner half of the bat to fine leg for a run.
Round the wicket, short of a length but wide outside off and John Campbell lets it go.
Change of ends for Lakmal! He replaces Vishwa Fernando!
Full and quick around off, Bonner keeps it out safely to end the over.

Chameera pulls his length back and bowls it on the pad. Campbell looks to flick this squarer than the previous ball. He misses and the ball goes behind square on the leg side off his thigh pad. He takes a leg bye.

FOUR! Great timing! Chameera is guilty of going too full and on the pads. Campbell does not try to hit it hard. He just times it and uses the pace of Dushmantha to flick it in front of square on the leg side. The outfield is very quick and the ball races away to the fence.
Full and pacy delivery outside off. Campbell lets that carry to the keeper.
Good length ball on middle and leg. Campbell defends it to the on side. Good start for Chameera. He has started with good pace and right line and length.
Chameera starts with a full ball on middle and off. Campbell defends it to mid off. Looks for a run but then quickly shouts a loud no to his partner.
First bowling change of the day. It sees Dushmantha Chameera (2-1-2-0) replace Suranga Lakmal!
Ahhh...poor delivery to finish. Short and going way down the leg side, it misses Nkrumah Bonner's attempted pull shot and is collected by the keeper.
He is getting the ball to move in the air here. Fires another yorker, which comes in towards the batsman and Bonner digs it out.
Brilliant yorker to follow. Right on his stumps and gets this one to swing in after pitching. Nkrumah Bonner does well to dig it out.
Excellent length and line. Length ball on off, gets this to come in with the angle as he is coming from over the wicket. Nkrumah Bonner manages to play it out.
Good cricket all round. Fullish ball on off and JC taps it to covers for a quick run.
Length ball, swinging away from the batter. He lets it go.

FOUR! Much better length and another fortuitous boundary for the hosts! Lakmal continues to target the off stump. This time he goes fuller, Bonner looks to defend but then decides to take his bat away. Too late though as the ball hits the outer half of his bat on its way up. Luckily for Nkrumah Bonner, it goes away from the man at gully and to the fence.

Good ball! Outside off and shaping away. Asking the batter to have a poke. Bonner initially looks to defend it away from his body but then takes his bat back inside. A couple of inches fuller and Lakmal could have had his man.
Good length ball on off, Nkrumah Bonner keeps his eyes on the ball and defends it right beneath his eyes to cover.
Fullish outside off. Lakmal wants Bonner to go for the drive but Nkrumah is happy to let it go to the keeper.
Follows the boundary with an astute defensive shot.

EDGED AND FOUR! Somehow Bonner finds the thinnest of gaps. Good length ball in the channel of uncertainty. Bonner is forced to have a poke at it. To his credit, he goes with soft hands, and hence the ball does not carry to the man in the slip cordon. It bounces and goes away through the gap between third slip and gully to the third man fence.
Good delivery to end the over. Back of a length, a bit closer to the stumps and it is punched away to mid off.
Short of a length, outside off. John Campbell looks to play it through the covers but gets the inside half of the bat as the ball rolls to mid off.
Fullish ball, on his stumps as JC plays a solid front foot punch back to the bowler.
Tap and run. Length ball, angling across his stumps and Nkrumah Bonner taps it to short cover for a run.
Fullish, pitching outside leg and defended.
Again, he is rapped on the pads. Good length delivery, on his pads and Nkrumah Bonner looks to work it away but misses his shot. Too high!

FOUR! Poor ball and rightfully punished! Too full and too straight on the pads. Campbell has no qualms in flicking it off his pad and showing his wrist work. He flicks it through square leg and the fielder from fine leg has no chance of cutting that out.
Full on middle. JC turns it with the movement but finds short fine leg.
Slightly shorter than a length ball on leg. Campbell looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the thigh pad.
Lakmal targets the stumps. Campbell continues to show his patience and blocks this too.
Length delivery on off, Campbell defends it towards mid on.
Good length ball around off, Campbell keeps it out.
Full ball on his stumps and Nkrumah Bonner solidly defends it off the front foot. Sri Lanka are not giving away easy runs to the batters.

Rapped on the pad yet again. Fuller length, on leg stump and misses the batter's leg glance to hit him on the pads. Big appeal but nothing from the umpire. No DRS taken. Good decision as the replay shows that the ball was pitching outside leg.
Rapped on the pads but pitching outside leg. Good length ball, outside leg and misses Nkrumah Bonner's flick to hit him on the pad.
Full, outside off and Nkrumah Bonner has no problem in letting it go.
Extra bit of pace there. Short of a length on leg stump, it hurries onto him but Nkrumah Bonner is able to keep it out.
Full, a bit straighter this time and John Campbell plays it to square leg for a run.

EDGED AND FOUR! Right between gully and third slip! Good length ball outside off, it shapes away from Bonner. He looks to defend it away from his body and does so with soft hands. The ball bisects gully and third slip and goes to the fence for a boundary, the first of the West Indian innings.
First real shot of intent this morning! Lakmal goes short on middle. Bonner pulls it over mid-wiciet. He does not time it well but there is no one in the deep. Two taken.
Full on middle, Bonner defends it to short mid-wicket.
Around the pads, Campbell tucks it to the on side and gets to the other end. He too gets his first run of the day.
First run of the day and it has come off the bat of Bonner! Full on off, Nkrumah taps it to covers and gets off the mark with a single.
Full and shaping away from outside off. Lakmal wants Campbell to go for the drive but he keeps his calm and leaves it alone.
Full delivery, outside off and John Campbell leaves it alone. Fourth over of the day and it is the fourth successive maiden.
Length ball, outside off as John Campbell lets it be.

A big slash by John Campbell but he misses it, the pressure seems to be building on the Windies. Short and wide outside off, Campbell looks to cut it away but does not move his feet at all, the ball goes past the bat.
Full ball, on the fourth stump. John Campbell leans into it to play it to cover-point.
Nice bounce there. Short of a length, outside off but this one rises on him and John Campbell plays it to point.
Short of a length, a bit wide outside off as John Campbell shoulders his arms.
Another maiden! This time it is a wicket maiden. Full and swinging away. Bonner leaves it alone to see off the over. Good over from Lakmal.
Another good ball! Lakmal continues to hit the deck hard on off. The ball shapes away a bit from the right-hander. Bonner defends it late off his back foot.
Length ball on off, Bonner gets on his back foot and keeps it out.
Good length ball on off, Bonner defends it.
Appeal but turned down! Looks to be going down! On the pads and high. Bonner looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the thigh pad. There is an appeal but the umpire is not keen.
Nkrumah Bonner walks out at number 3! He batted a position down in his debut series last month and got handy scores of 17, 86, 90 and 38. Can he do wonders in his first home Test?

OUT! CAUGHT! Early breakthrough for Sri Lanka on Day 2! Just what the doctor ordered for the visitors. The experience of Lakmal gets the better of the West Indies skipper. Good length ball wide outside off, Kraigg Brathwaite is tempted to have a poke at it. He cannot control his temptation and goes for it but ends up getting a thick outside edge that goes low to second slip. Dhananjaya de Silva there manages to take a good sharp catch. An avoidable shot for Kraigg, against his nature, he got lured into it and ended up playing away from his body.
Good delivery to finish the over. Full, on off and John Campbell pushes this to mid off. Dot ball.
Short of a length, outside off and John Campbell lets this go.
Good area again. Fullish on off and John Campbell leans into it to play it to covers.
Beaten! Excellent delivery, this. Fuller, on the fourth stump and forces John Campbell to play at it. He is beaten as the ball shapes away after pitching.
Back of a length and outside off, John Campbell goes on his back foot and plays it to point.
Vishwa Fernando starts with a fuller ball on middle and John Campbell defends it to short mid-wicket.
Who will bowl from the other end? It will be Vishwa Fernando.
Full ball to end the over. It is on off, the West Indies skipper defends it to see it off.
Lakmal goes outside off now and tempts Brathwaite to drive but he is happy to let it go to the keeper.
Lakmal continues to ask questions in the first over by bowling the off stump line. Brathwaite defends it.
Good length delivery pitching around off. Brathwaite shuffles across his stumps a bit and defends this towards mid on.
Good length ball on off. Brathwaite defends this one.
Lakmal starts the day with a good length ball pitching on off and shaping away just a little. Brathwaite begins by getting behind the line and blocking it.

Time to get underway! Kraigg Brathwaite and John Campbell are the overnight pair for West Indies. The conditions are bright and sunny, looking like a good day for batting. Expect some early movement though. Here is Suranga Lakmal running in...

Pitch report - The surface has dried out and there is not a lot of moisture left. There are not a lot of indentations on it which means that it's quite firm. Stroke making will be easy but at the same time, the bowlers might get some assistance in the morning session. Pitching the ball up will be the key for Sri Lanka.

Nkrumah Bonner comes up for a chat! Says that it was a great team performance on Day 1 and they applied pressure on Sri Lanka. Praises Jason Holder and Kemar Roach for their efforts. Adds that as a batsman you should be ready to bat at any position and nothing much changes. Tells us that it's special for him to play at home and he is excited to make West Indies proud. Feels that the wicket was slow in the morning and it quickened up in the afternoon. He is hoping the pitch to be at its best today.

In case you missed the action on Day 1, let's give you a small recap. Toss was won by West Indies and they won everything after that as well. Asked to bat first, the Lankan openers started watchfully and batted for around 11 overs without giving anything to the home team. However, once the first wicket fell, things quickly unravelled and soon the touring party got reduced to three wickets by Lunch. Another couple of wickets fell in the afternoon session although Lahiru Thirimanne continued to fight strongly. But his resistance was also put to rest in the evening session and the Lankan tail didn't last long.
